quotes.text: In plain English, dataverse is Microsoft's cloud data platform for business information. It stores that information, in structured tables. So the data has a clear shape, instead of living as random notes, loose files, and disconnected spreadsheet tabs.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines Dataverse in plain language and explains why structured tables matter.

quotes.text: Instead of asking, how do we sync these two customer lists? You can ask which people and apps need to work with this customer record and what should each of them be allowed to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Dynamics 365 integration from data syncing to shared access and permissions.

quotes.text: That means access doesn't depend on somebody remembering which buttons to hide in every app. The permissions sit with the data itself.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why security in Dataverse is attached to the data rather than to individual apps.

quotes.text: This matters because you don't want one app accepting incomplete data while another app rejects it. The rule belongs with the business information, not with one screen that happens to show it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes a clear design argument for placing business rules at the data layer.

quotes.text: Choose Dataverse when multiple people and apps need to work with connected business data. You need clear access rules and repeatable processes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a simple decision rule for when Dataverse is the right choice.

takeaways: Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service already store their data in Dataverse, so integration is mostly about shared tables and access rather than syncing two systems.

Dataverse organizes business data in standard and custom tables with rows, columns and relationships, protected by Entra ID identity, security roles, column-level security, business units and business rules.
Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI can work on the same Dataverse rows, while Excel, SharePoint lists and SQL remain better fits for personal analysis, simple tracking or deep developer control.
hook: When the same customer lives in five spreadsheets and tools, nobody knows which copy to trust. This episode is for business users, makers and Dynamics 365 teams who want to understand what Dataverse is and how Dynamics 365 actually uses it. You will learn how tables, security and rules form one shared foundation that Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI can build on without extra copies.
